pr_title: editor: Highlight all matching occurrences of text in selection
pr_body:
Closes #12635

- [x] Get it working
- [x] Disable for multi cursor
- [x] Disable for vim visual line selection
- [x] Add setting to disable it
- [x] Add scrollbar marker
- [x] Handle delete state capturing selection

Preview:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a76cde64-4f6c-4575-91cc-3a03a954e7a9

Release Notes:

- Added support to highlight all matching occurrences of text within the selection in editor.
pr_comments: @0xtimsb thanks for working on this. One suggestion: please add markers on the scrollbar on the right not just for where the cursor is at but also where the highlighted text is. The benefit is quickly identifying text anywhere in the editor, not just the area visible in the window. I am not describing anything new, this is how it is done in VSC. Thanks again
Looks great! But yes, please add the scrollbar occurrences view. Massive help when identifying these tokens. Many thanks!

comments: Hey @hoanganh2303 - I'm not entirely sure I understand what you are looking for - does this feature exist in another editor? If so, could you share a screenshot here?

Related discussion: 
- https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/discussions/9238 .

Hi I’m new to Zed and also came looking for this solution.

In Atom you could double-click to highlight a string/variable. Atom will highlight **all** occurrences in the file. 

Zed only highlights a variable within its scope. 
Not in the entire file, and doesn’t work on strings etc.

Yeah this is the sole reason I've not switched entirely to Zed for small scripts and viewing the odd files that VSCode would be too cumbersome for.
Its incredibly useful to be able to see other occurences of names/variables/tokens just by highlighting one of them.

> Yeah this is the sole reason I've not switched entirely to Zed for small scripts and viewing the odd files that VSCode would be too cumbersome for. Its incredibly useful to be able to see other occurences of names/variables/tokens just by highlighting one of them.

2. Cmd + F (find)

@g0t4 to answer your questions:

1. Yes, it currently only works for a single line. Ideally, we should handle multiple lines in case of wrapping.
2. We have a default debounce time of `50 ms` for this. If you'd like it to happen in real-time, setting it to `0` will do the trick.
3. Hmm, gotta check out [visimatch.nvim](https://github.com/wurli/visimatch.nvim).

I'm not actively addressing the above mentioned points right now, but I'll eventually get to them as time allows or if an issue comes up.
